text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Syrian President Hafez al-Assad says he still is confident that U.S. President Bill Clinton wants peace and is able to achieve it.

- President Hosni Mubarak receives a letter from King Hussein of Jordan before the start of the joint committee of the two countries. The committee will meet today in Cairo and six agreements will be signed in fields including culture and electricity.
- Minister for Supply and Trade Ahmed Gueily said that Egypt and the United States on Monday will discuss setting up a free trade zone to increase their trade.
- U.S. political source in Washington says Israeli-Palestinian talks are expected to resume shortly.
- Informed source says that the government plans to implement the land law governing relations between owners and renters without any side effects and to benefit both sides.

- Mubarak said it was not true that British beef had been imported via Belgium. He said that Egyptian markets are free of any imported beef stricken with mad cow disease after authorities took steps to prevent it.
